# package pdo

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/pdo"
```

Package pdo implements CANopen process data objects (CiA 301 7.2.2, 7.5.2.35..38): mapping entries and the bit-exact packing of mapped values, the transmit and receive PDOs of a device, and a master's tools to configure a node's PDOs over SDO and to decode and produce PDOs.

#### Mapping {#hdr-Mapping}

A mapping entry ([Entry](#type-entry)) is the UNSIGNED32 index\<\<16 | sub-index\<\<8 | length in bits. Mapped values are packed little-endian, least significant bit first, one after the other with no padding ([Pack](#func-pack), [Unpack](#func-unpack)); lengths need not be multiples of 8 (a BOOLEAN takes one bit). A classical PDO carries at most 64 bits; a CANopen FD PDO up to 512 (below). [ValidateEntry](#func-validateentry) decides what can be mapped; in short: an existing, PDO-mappable object, readable for a TPDO and writable for an RPDO, mapped with its data type's length (a BOOLEAN with 1 or 8 bits), or in an RPDO a dummy entry (data types 0x0001..0x0007).

#### Device side {#hdr-Device_side}

[TPDO](#type-tpdo) and [RPDO](#type-rpdo) bind to a dictionary built with od.Standard (or any dictionary with the 0x1400/0x1600/0x1800/0x1A00 objects): they read their configuration from it, follow its changes, and install write hooks ([Protect](#func-protect)) that enforce the reconfiguration rules, mirroring CANopenNode v4 (CO\_PDO.c):

  - a PDO is active when its COB-ID is valid and something is mapped; a valid COB-ID cannot be written while nothing is mapped.
  - the mapping can only change while the PDO is not active, entries only while sub 00h is 0: otherwise abort 0x06010000.
  - entries are checked when written and again when sub 00h is set.
  - the identifier of an active PDO cannot change (0x06090030), nor its inhibit time or SYNC start value; reserved transmission types are refused (0x06090030).

Deviations from CANopenNode: 29-bit COB-IDs are accepted (bit 29); sub-bytes mappings (a BOOLEAN with 1 bit, any non-byte-aligned layout) are supported where CANopenNode only maps whole bytes; mapping lengths shorter than the data type (CANopenNode allows them) are refused; dummy entries are refused in TPDOs (CiA 301 defines them for RPDOs); TPDO types 252 and 253 are implemented; RPDOs enforce the SYNC window (below).

A mapping sub-index 00h of FEh or FFh marks a multiplexed PDO (MPDO, CiA 301): [Load](#func-load) reports it in [Config.MPDO](#func-config-mpdo) with no entries, the write hooks accept it while the PDO is not active, and the classical services treat the PDO as inactive (the mpdo package serves it).

Both services transmit and receive only while enabled (the node calls SetEnabled on entering and leaving NMT operational) and take SYNC through OnSync, which the node wires to its SYNC consumer.

#### SYNC window {#hdr-SYNC_window}

The synchronous window length (0x1007, µs; 0 disables it) bounds synchronous PDOs after each SYNC. CiA 301's description of 0x1007 (as device manuals quote it, e.g. Nanotec's object 1007h page: synchronous TPDOs are rejected once the window expired, RPDOs until the next SYNC) is implemented as follows:

  - TPDO (types 0..240): the data are sampled at the SYNC and sent within the window, the send being bounded by it; a PDO not sent before the window closes is discarded ([TPDOStats.WindowMissed](#func-tpdostats-windowmissed)). CANopenNode does the same by clearing pending synchronous TPDOs when CO\_SYNC\_process reports CO\_SYNC\_PASSED\_WINDOW (CANopen.c: CO\_CANclearPendingSyncPDOs).
  - RPDO (types 0..240): a PDO received after the window of the last SYNC closed is discarded ([RPDOStats.OutsideWindow](#func-rpdostats-outsidewindow)) until the next SYNC; one received within it is applied on the next SYNC as usual. CANopenNode does not check the window for RPDOs.

OnSync reads 0x1007 from the dictionary and measures the window from the call; OnSyncWindow takes the window end from the caller (the syncobj.Event's WindowEnd, measured from the frame's receive time). [WithClock](#func-withclock) replaces the clock for tests.

#### CANopen FD {#hdr-CANopen_FD}

With [WithFD](#func-withfd) a PDO is a CANopen FD PDO (CiA 1301): sent in a CAN FD frame (BRS selectable) with up to 64 data bytes, its mapping limited to MaxBitsFD (512) bits instead of MaxBits — still at most 64 entries (sub-indices 01h..40h) — and validated so by the write hooks ([ProtectFD](#func-protectfd)). Public sources (CiA's CANopen FD pages and poster, the HMS/Ixxat CANopen FD whitepaper, emotas, Kvaser, MicroControl) establish that CANopen FD PDOs carry 1 to 64 bytes in CAN FD data frames, that the PDO communication and mapping objects keep their indices and sub-indices (01h COB-ID, 02h transmission type, 03h inhibit time, 05h event timer, 06h SYNC start value), and that CANopen FD has no remote frames. They describe no per-PDO FD or BRS flag (CiA states that CANopen FD uses the CAN FD frame format for all its protocols, without distinguishing bit rate switching), so the choice is an option. Consequences, which are interpretations of this library:

  - CAN FD lengths above 8 come in steps (12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64): a TPDO is padded with zeros to the next one, and an RPDO accepts a frame up to that length without reporting "length exceeded" (0x8220).
  - no remote transmission requests: an FD TPDO does not subscribe to them; types 252/253 sample but never transmit; [Listener.Request](#func-listener-request) fails with ErrNoRTR. COB-ID bit 30 is kept but has no effect.

Classical PDOs (without the option) behave exactly as before.

#### Master side {#hdr-Master_side}

[Configure](#func-configure) writes a node's PDO configuration over an [SDO](#type-sdo) in the CiA 301 order and [ReadConfig](#func-readconfig) reads it back. A [Decoder](#type-decoder) (with a [Listener](#type-listener)) turns a node's PDOs into named values, using a dictionary that describes the node (for example built from its EDS); an [Encoder](#type-encoder) (with a [Sender](#type-sender)) produces PDOs for it.

```go
const (

	// the 8 data bytes of a classical CAN frame.
	MaxBits = 64

	// MaxBitsFD is the largest total length of the mapped objects of a
```

### func CommIndex

```go
func CommIndex(transmit bool, n int) uint16
```

CommIndex returns the index of the communication parameter of TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n (1..512); 0, which is no PDO parameter, for n out of range.

### func Configure

```go
func Configure(ctx context.Context, sdo SDO, transmit bool, n int, cfg Config) error
```

Configure writes the configuration of TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n of a remote node with the sequence of CiA 301 7.5.2.36/38:

 1. invalidate: COB-ID with bit 31 set (and the new identifier)
 2. disable the mapping: sub 00h of the mapping = 0
 3. write the mapping entries
 4. enable the mapping: sub 00h = number of entries (or cfg.MPDO, FEh or FFh, for a multiplexed PDO without entries)
 5. transmission type, inhibit time (TPDO), event timer, SYNC start value (TPDO)
 6. if cfg.COBID is valid: the COB-ID, which makes the PDO valid

Inhibit time, event timer and SYNC start value are skipped when they are 0 and the node lacks them. The first failure stops the sequence; the error names the object and wraps the SDO error (an [canopen.AbortCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortCode) for a refused write).

### func Pack

```go
func Pack(m Mapping, values [][]byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Pack packs values, one per entry in the encoding of the object's data type (little-endian, as [canopen.Encode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#Encode) returns it), into PDO data of [Mapping.Len](#func-mapping-len) bytes. Each value contributes its low Bits bits, least significant first, at the bit position following the previous entry's. A nil value (for dummy entries, say) packs as zeros. Mappings longer than MaxBits are refused with [canopen.AbortPDOLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortPDOLength); [PackFD](#func-packfd) takes CANopen FD mappings.

### func PackFD

```go
func PackFD(m Mapping, values [][]byte) ([]byte, error)
```

PackFD packs the values of a CANopen FD PDO as [Pack](#func-pack) does, for mappings of up to MaxBitsFD bits.

### func Protect

```go
func Protect(d *od.Dictionary, transmit bool, n int) (unprotect func(), err error)
```

Protect installs write hooks on the communication and mapping parameters of TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n of a dictionary, so that remote writes (from an SDO server) follow the reconfiguration rules of CiA 301 7.5.2.35..38 as CANopenNode enforces them. "Active" below is [Config.Active](#func-config-active): COB-ID valid and at least one mapped object.

Communication parameter:

  - sub 01h (COB-ID): bits 11..28 of an 11-bit COB-ID set, a valid COB-ID with a restricted identifier ([Restricted](#func-restricted)), changing the identifier (or its format) of an active PDO, or making the COB-ID valid while nothing is mapped: [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue).
  - sub 02h (transmission type): reserved types (241..251, and 252/253 for an RPDO): [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue).
  - sub 03h (inhibit time) and 06h (SYNC start value) of a TPDO while it is active, and a SYNC start value above 240: [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue).

Mapping parameter:

  - any write while the PDO is active, and a write of an entry (sub ≥ 1) while sub 00h is not 0: [canopen.AbortUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortUnsupported) (CANopenNode's ODR\_UNSUPP\_ACCESS).
  - an entry other than 0 that [ValidateEntry](#func-validateentry) refuses: its code ([canopen.AbortNoObject](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNoObject) or [canopen.AbortNotMappable](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNotMappable)).
  - sub 00h FEh or FFh (MPDO, CiA 301) is accepted as 0 is, without checking entries; the PDO is then inactive for [TPDO](#type-tpdo) and [RPDO](#type-rpdo).
  - sub 00h above the number of entries or MaxEntries, or entries longer than MaxBits in total: [canopen.AbortPDOLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortPDOLength); an entry 1..n that is invalid: its [ValidateEntry](#func-validateentry) code.

A value wider than the CiA 301 data type of its sub-object (possible only with a dictionary that declares it wider) is refused: a COB-ID or transmission type with [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue), a mapping entry with [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue) when written and [canopen.AbortNotMappable](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNotMappable) when enabled by sub 00h. A stored COB-ID above 32 bits counts as invalid.

Local writes ([od.Dictionary.Set](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Set)) are not checked. The returned unprotect function removes the hooks (later calls do nothing); installing them twice is harmless. [NewTPDO](#func-newtpdo) and [NewRPDO](#func-newrpdo) call Protect, and their Close calls unprotect.

### func Unpack

```go
func Unpack(m Mapping, data []byte) ([][]byte, error)
```

Unpack splits PDO data into the values of the entries: each value has Bits/8 bytes rounded up, little-endian, which for every mappable length is the encoding of the object's data type (a 1-bit BOOLEAN is one byte, 0 or 1). Data beyond the mapping is ignored; data shorter than the mapping is an error wrapping ErrLength. Mappings longer than MaxBits are refused with [canopen.AbortPDOLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortPDOLength); [UnpackFD](#func-unpackfd) takes CANopen FD mappings.

### func UnpackFD

```go
func UnpackFD(m Mapping, data []byte) ([][]byte, error)
```

UnpackFD splits the data of a CANopen FD PDO as [Unpack](#func-unpack) does, for mappings of up to MaxBitsFD bits.

### func ValidateEntry

```go
func ValidateEntry(d *od.Dictionary, e Entry, transmit bool) error
```

ValidateEntry checks one mapping entry of a TPDO (transmit) or an RPDO against a dictionary and returns the SDO abort code a write of it gets:

  - [canopen.AbortNoObject](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNoObject): the object or sub-object does not exist
  - [canopen.AbortNotMappable](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortNotMappable): a zero length; the object is not PDO-mappable, not readable (TPDO) or not writable (RPDO); a dummy entry in a TPDO; a length that differs from the data type's

The length must be the data type's [canopen.DataType.Bits](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#DataType.Bits); a BOOLEAN may be mapped with 1 bit (CiA 301) or 8 bits (as tools that only map whole bytes write it). Variable-length types cannot be mapped. Dummy entries (data types 0x0001..0x0007) are accepted in RPDOs only, with their type's length; the dictionary need not hold the type objects.

## Types

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// COBID is sub-index 01h: the CAN identifier, bit 31 invalid, bit 30
	// no RTR allowed (TPDO), bit 29 29-bit identifier.
	COBID canopen.COBID
	// TransmissionType is sub-index 02h.
	TransmissionType TransmissionType
	// InhibitTime is sub-index 03h, in units of 100 µs (TPDO).
	InhibitTime uint16
	// EventTimer is sub-index 05h in ms: the TPDO event timer, or the
	// RPDO deadline (0 disables it).
	EventTimer uint16
	// SyncStart is sub-index 06h of a TPDO: the SYNC counter value of the
	// first transmission of a cyclic synchronous TPDO (0 disables it).
	SyncStart uint8
	// Mapping lists the mapped objects (sub-index 00h is their number).
	Mapping Mapping
	// MPDO is the value of mapping sub-index 00h when it marks the PDO as
	// a multiplexed PDO (CiA 301: [MPDOSourceAddressing] FEh,
	// [MPDODestinationAddressing] FFh), and 0 otherwise. An MPDO has no
	// mapping entries and is inactive for the classical TPDO and RPDO
	// services (the mpdo package serves it).
	MPDO uint8
}
```

Config is the configuration of a PDO: its communication parameter (0x1400.. for RPDOs, 0x1800.. for TPDOs) and its mapping (0x1600.., 0x1A00..).

#### func Load

```go
func Load(d *od.Dictionary, transmit bool, n int) (Config, error)
```

Load reads the configuration of TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n from a dictionary with local reads (no access checks or hooks). Optional sub-indices (inhibit time, event timer, SYNC start value) that the dictionary lacks read as 0. A value wider than its data type (a COB-ID or mapping entry above 32 bits, a transmission type or SYNC start value above 8, inhibit time or event timer above 16) is an error wrapping [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue). It does not validate the mapping.

#### func ReadConfig

```go
func ReadConfig(ctx context.Context, sdo SDO, transmit bool, n int) (Config, error)
```

ReadConfig reads the configuration of TPDO (transmit) or RPDO n of a remote node. Inhibit time, event timer and SYNC start value read as 0 when the node does not have them. A value wider than its data type is an error wrapping [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue), as for [Load](#func-load).


Active reports whether a PDO with this configuration exists on the bus: the COB-ID is valid and at least one object is mapped. (A valid COB-ID with an empty mapping is how CiA 301 default configurations leave unused PDOs; like CANopenNode, the PDO then sends and receives nothing.)

#### func WithFD

```go
func WithFD(brs bool) Option
```

WithFD makes the PDO a CANopen FD PDO (CiA 1301): it is sent in CAN FD frames (with bit rate switching when brs is true), padded with zeros to the next valid CAN FD length, and its mapping may total up to MaxBitsFD bits (64 bytes). CiA 1301 runs every service of a CANopen FD network in CAN FD frames and has no per-PDO FD flag in the dictionary, so the choice is an option, normally the same for all PDOs of a device. Remote frames do not exist in CAN FD: an FD TPDO answers no remote request (types 252 and 253 therefore never transmit), and [Listener.Request](#func-listener-request) fails with ErrNoRTR. An FD RPDO also accepts classical frames; its length check allows the CAN FD padding (a mapping of 9 bytes arrives in a 12-byte frame). Applies to [TPDO](#type-tpdo), [RPDO](#type-rpdo), [NewDecoder](#func-newdecoder), [NewEncoder](#func-newencoder) (and so [Sender](#type-sender) and [Listener](#type-listener)) and [ProtectFD](#func-protectfd)-style validation of the services.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger (default: discard).

#### func WithReceiveHandler

```go
func WithReceiveHandler(f func(data []byte)) Option
```

WithReceiveHandler sets a function an [RPDO](#type-rpdo) calls after it has written the data of a received PDO to the dictionary (for synchronous types, on the SYNC that applies it), with the PDO data. It is called from the goroutine that wrote the dictionary: the service goroutine, or the caller of [RPDO.OnSync](#func-rpdo-onsync).

### type RPDO

```go
type RPDO struct {

	// synchronous: the PDO waiting for the SYNC

	// deadline monitoring running
	// deadline missed, reported
	// active length error code

	// end of the synchronous window of the last SYNC; zero: none

}
```

RPDO is a receive PDO of a device: it reads its parameters from the communication (0x1400+n-1) and mapping (0x1600+n-1) objects of a dictionary, follows their changes, and writes the values of received PDOs to the mapped objects with remote writes (so the dictionary's write hooks, limits and watchers apply; a refused object is counted and the others are still written). Dummy entries skip their bits.

Event-driven RPDOs (254, 255) are written when they arrive. Synchronous ones (0..240) are buffered and written on the next SYNC ([RPDO.OnSync](#func-rpdo-onsync)); a newer PDO before the SYNC replaces the buffered one. With a synchronous window (object 0x1007, µs, of the dictionary) a synchronous PDO that arrives after the window of the last SYNC has closed is discarded until the next SYNC, as CiA 301 describes object 0x1007 (and device manuals quoting it, e.g. Nanotec's "RxPDOs are rejected until the next SYNC"); it is counted in [RPDOStats.OutsideWindow](#func-rpdostats-outsidewindow). Before the first SYNC there is no window. CANopenNode does not check the window for RPDOs (CO\_PDO.c ignores it): this is a deliberate difference. The discarded PDO still counts as received for deadline monitoring and the length check.

A CANopen FD RPDO ([WithFD](#func-withfd)) takes mappings of up to 512 bits; frames padded to the next CAN FD length are not "too long".

A PDO shorter than the mapping is discarded and reported with EMCY code 0x8210; a longer one is used (its first bytes) and reported with 0x8220, as CANopenNode does (CiA 301 only requires reporting it). The event timer is the deadline monitor: when it is non-zero, the time between two PDOs is monitored from the first PDO received after the RPDO was enabled or reconfigured, and an expiry is reported once with 0x8250. Errors go to the [WithErrorHandler](#func-witherrorhandler) function, which also learns when they are resolved.

### type TPDO

```go
type TPDO struct {

	// SYNCs counted towards the next cyclic transmission
	// waiting for the SYNC start value
	// type 0: an event since the last SYNC; 1..240: RTR pending
	// 254/255: a transmission is due
	// 254/255: a mapped object changed

	// event timer deadline

}
```

TPDO is a transmit PDO of a device: it reads its parameters from the communication (0x1800+n-1) and mapping (0x1A00+n-1) objects of a dictionary, follows their changes, and sends the mapped values according to the transmission type:

  - 0 (synchronous acyclic): on the SYNC after an event ([TPDO.Trigger](#func-tpdo-trigger), a change of a mapped object, a remote request).
  - 1\..240 (synchronous cyclic): on every nth SYNC; with a SYNC start value s > 0 and SYNCs that carry a counter, the first transmission is on the SYNC with counter s. A remote request is answered on the next SYNC.
  - 252: sampled on every SYNC, sent on a remote request.
  - 253: sampled and sent on a remote request.
  - 254, 255 (event-driven): on an event — a change of a mapped object (the dictionary's watchers; a write of an unchanged value is not sent), [TPDO.Trigger](#func-tpdo-trigger), a remote request, the event timer expiring, or the service being enabled — no sooner than the inhibit time after the previous transmission. The event timer restarts with every transmission.

Synchronous transmissions (types 0..240) are made only within the synchronous window after the SYNC (object 0x1007, µs, of the dictionary; 0 or absent: no window): a PDO sampled at the SYNC but not sent before the window closes is discarded and counted in [TPDOStats.WindowMissed](#func-tpdostats-windowmissed), as CiA 301 and CANopenNode (which clears the pending synchronous TPDOs when the window passes, CO\_SYNC.c/CANopen.c) do. The send is bounded by the window: a bus that cannot take the frame in time drops it.

Remote requests are answered unless COB-ID bit 30 is set or the PDO is a CANopen FD PDO ([WithFD](#func-withfd): CAN FD has no remote frames). The TPDO transmits only while enabled ([TPDO.SetEnabled](#func-tpdo-setenabled): NMT operational) and active ([Config.Active](#func-config-active)). Mapped objects are read with remote reads, so read hooks may supply values. SYNC reaches the TPDO through [TPDO.OnSync](#func-tpdo-onsync), which the node wires to its SYNC consumer.

A synchronous transmission not made before windowEnd is discarded and counted in [TPDOStats.WindowMissed](#func-tpdostats-windowmissed).

```go

```

Transmit reads the mapped objects and sends the TPDO now, whatever its transmission type and inhibit time. It fails with ErrDisabled or ErrInactive when the TPDO cannot be sent.

#### func (TPDO) Trigger

```go
func (t *TPDO) Trigger()
```

Trigger signals an application event: an event-driven TPDO is sent (no sooner than its inhibit time allows), a synchronous acyclic one on the next SYNC. Other types ignore it.

```go
type TPDOStats struct {
	Sent        uint64 `json:"sent"`        // PDOs transmitted
	SendErrors  uint64 `json:"sendErrors"`  // transmissions the bus refused
	ReadErrors  uint64 `json:"readErrors"`  // transmissions skipped: a mapped object could not be read
	Unchanged   uint64 `json:"unchanged"`   // change events with unchanged data, not sent
	Syncs       uint64 `json:"syncs"`       // SYNCs seen while enabled and active
	RTRs        uint64 `json:"rtrs"`        // remote transmission requests received

	// synchronous window (0x1007) closed before they were sent.

}
```

TPDOStats counts what a [TPDO](#type-tpdo) did.

### type TransmissionType

```go
type TransmissionType uint8
```

TransmissionType is the transmission type of a PDO (sub-index 02h of the communication parameter, CiA 301 7.5.2.35 and 7.5.2.37).

```go
const (
	// TransSyncAcyclic (0): a TPDO is sent on the SYNC after an event; an
	// RPDO is applied on the next SYNC.
	TransSyncAcyclic TransmissionType = 0
	// TransSyncMax (240) is the largest cyclic synchronous type.
	TransSyncMax TransmissionType = 240
	// TransRTRSync (252, TPDO only): the data are sampled on SYNC and sent
	// on a remote transmission request.
	TransRTRSync TransmissionType = 252
	// TransRTR (253, TPDO only): the data are sampled and sent on a remote
	// transmission request.
	TransRTR TransmissionType = 253
	// TransEventManufacturer (254): event-driven, the event being
	// manufacturer-specific.
	TransEventManufacturer TransmissionType = 254
	// TransEventProfile (255): event-driven, the event being defined by
	// the device or application profile.
	TransEventProfile TransmissionType = 255
)
```

Transmission types. 1..240 are cyclic synchronous: a TPDO is sent on every nth SYNC, an RPDO is applied on the next SYNC. 241..251 are reserved.
